discovery: Invention and development of the superconducting nanowire single-photon detector (SNSPD)

nominees.name: Gregory N. Gol'tsman
nominees.affiliation: Moscow Pedagogical State University / HSE University, Moscow

nominees.name: Sae Woo Nam
nominees.affiliation: National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST), Boulder

motivation: In 2001 Gol'tsman, Sobolewski and collaborators showed that a current-biased ultrathin superconducting NbN nanowire registers single photons through a local hotspot that switches it out of the superconducting state. Nam and the NIST group then turned this into a practical technology, reaching system detection efficiencies above 90%, picosecond timing jitter, very low dark counts and high count rates across ultraviolet to mid-infrared wavelengths. SNSPDs now set the standard for single-photon detection. They made loophole-free Bell tests possible, along with long-distance quantum key distribution, entanglement distribution and teleportation over fibre networks, deep-space optical communication and photonic quantum computing. They are now moving into searches for dark matter and for new particles. Few instruments have opened up so many new experiments. Physicists could not see these things before, and now they can.
